_notice: SAMPLE CONTENT: illustrative demo cases written for this app. They must be reviewed or replaced by the team's clinical supervisor and are not validated assessment material. To enable scoring, add an "answer_index" (0-based index into options) to each question.

phases.title: Acute & Emergency Care
phases.description: Time-critical presentations in the emergency setting.

phases.title: Systems Medicine
phases.description: Neurology, hepatology, gastroenterology, nephrology and rheumatology.

phases.title: Women, Children & Community Health
phases.description: Paediatrics, obstetrics, gynaecology, dermatology, infectious disease and psychiatry.

questions.title: Chest pain in a smoker
questions.vignette: A 58-year-old man who smokes presents with 40 minutes of crushing retrosternal chest pain radiating to the left arm, with sweating and nausea. BP 104/68 mmHg, HR 56/min. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Breathlessness after a long flight
questions.vignette: A 26-year-old woman on the combined oral contraceptive pill develops sudden pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness a day after a 12-hour flight. HR 118/min, SpO2 91% on air, chest clear on auscultation. Her right calf is swollen and tender.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Vomiting in a young diabetic
questions.vignette: A 19-year-old man with type 1 diabetes presents with vomiting, abdominal pain and deep sighing respirations after missing insulin doses during a viral illness. Capillary glucose 480 mg/dL, arterial pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9 mmol/L, urine ketones 3+.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Fever after forest travel
questions.vignette: A 34-year-old man returned from a forested, mosquito-endemic area 10 days ago. He reports fever with rigors and drenching sweats recurring every 48 hours. Examination shows pallor and a palpable spleen. Hb 9.2 g/dL, platelets 96,000/µL.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Sudden arm weakness
questions.vignette: A 67-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation, not on anticoagulation, develops sudden weakness of the right arm and face and difficulty producing words, beginning 1 hour ago. BP 168/94 mmHg, capillary glucose 112 mg/dL.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Acute ischaemic stroke (left middle cerebral artery territory)

questions.title: Migrating abdominal pain
questions.vignette: A 22-year-old man has periumbilical pain that has moved to the right iliac fossa over 12 hours, with anorexia and one episode of vomiting. Temperature 37.9 °C, tenderness and rebound at McBurney's point. WBC 14,200/µL.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Colicky loin pain
questions.vignette: A 45-year-old man presents with sudden, severe colicky left loin pain radiating to the groin. He is restless and cannot find a comfortable position. He is afebrile; urinalysis shows microscopic haematuria and no nitrites.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Fatigue and heavy periods
questions.vignette: A 30-year-old woman reports fatigue, breathlessness on stairs and craving ice. She has heavy menstrual periods. Examination shows pallor and spoon-shaped nails. Hb 8.5 g/dL, MCV 68 fL, serum ferritin 6 ng/mL.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Weight loss and palpitations
questions.vignette: A 35-year-old woman reports weight loss despite good appetite, heat intolerance, palpitations and tremor for 3 months. She has a diffuse goitre with a bruit and bilateral proptosis. TSH is suppressed and free T4 is raised.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Chronic cough in a smoker
questions.vignette: A 62-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history has progressive exertional breathlessness and a productive cough every winter for the last 3 years. He has a hyperinflated chest. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC is 0.58 with minimal reversibility.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Night-time breathlessness
questions.vignette: A 72-year-old man with prior myocardial infarction wakes at night acutely breathless and has to sit upright. He has bibasal crackles, raised JVP, bilateral pitting ankle oedema and a third heart sound. NT-proBNP is markedly raised.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Tearing chest pain
questions.vignette: A 55-year-old hypertensive man has sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back between the shoulder blades. BP is 182/100 mmHg in the right arm and 138/80 mmHg in the left. Chest X-ray shows a widened mediastinum.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Sudden pleuritic pain at rest
questions.vignette: A tall, thin 24-year-old man develops sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness while sitting at his desk. The right hemithorax has reduced breath sounds and is hyper-resonant to percussion. SpO2 95%.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Collapse after a snack
questions.vignette: Minutes after eating a peanut-containing snack, a 19-year-old woman develops lip swelling, generalised urticaria, wheeze and light-headedness. BP 80/50 mmHg, HR 128/min.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Epigastric pain after a binge
questions.vignette: A 40-year-old man with heavy alcohol use presents with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, starting after a weekend binge, with repeated vomiting. He leans forward for relief. Serum lipase is five times the upper limit of normal.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Fever, headache and rash
questions.vignette: A 28-year-old man has had fever, severe headache, photophobia and vomiting for 12 hours. He has neck stiffness, a positive Kernig's sign and a non-blanching petechial rash on the legs. BP 96/60 mmHg.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Thunderclap headache
questions.vignette: A 50-year-old woman develops a sudden, severe 'worst-ever' headache while lifting weights, followed by a brief loss of consciousness. She now has neck stiffness and photophobia but no fever. GCS 14.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Confusion in an insulin user
questions.vignette: A 68-year-old man with type 2 diabetes on insulin is found confused, sweaty and tremulous after skipping lunch. HR 110/min, no focal neurological signs. Capillary glucose is 42 mg/dL.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Farmer found unwell
questions.vignette: A 33-year-old farmer is brought in after ingesting an unknown substance kept in the field shed. He has pinpoint pupils, profuse salivation, lacrimation, bronchorrhoea, bradycardia and muscle fasciculations.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Hypotension with fever
questions.vignette: A 75-year-old woman with two days of dysuria and frequency is now confused. Temperature 39.2 °C, HR 124/min, BP 82/50 mmHg despite 30 mL/kg IV fluids, serum lactate 4.5 mmol/L.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Septic shock from a urinary source

questions.title: Relapsing neurological symptoms
questions.vignette: A 26-year-old woman had an episode of painful blurred vision in one eye two years ago that resolved. She now has numbness of both legs and electric-shock sensations down the spine on neck flexion. MRI shows periventricular white-matter lesions.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Ascending weakness
questions.vignette: A 35-year-old man develops symmetrical weakness starting in the legs and ascending over 5 days, two weeks after a diarrhoeal illness. Reflexes are absent. CSF shows raised protein with a normal cell count.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Tremor and slowness
questions.vignette: A 64-year-old man has a resting 'pill-rolling' tremor of the right hand, slowness of movement, cogwheel rigidity and a shuffling gait with reduced arm swing. He takes no regular medications.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Itching and fatigue
questions.vignette: A 45-year-old woman has generalised itching and fatigue for 6 months. Liver tests show a markedly raised alkaline phosphatase and GGT with normal bilirubin. Antimitochondrial antibody is strongly positive. Ultrasound shows no biliary dilatation.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Jaundice and abdominal swelling
questions.vignette: A 52-year-old man with long-standing heavy alcohol use has jaundice, a distended abdomen with shifting dullness, spider naevi and palmar erythema. Albumin 2.4 g/dL, INR 1.9. Ultrasound shows a small nodular liver.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Bloody diarrhoea
questions.vignette: A 23-year-old man has 3 months of diarrhoea with blood and mucus, urgency and tenesmus. Stool cultures are negative. Colonoscopy shows continuous mucosal inflammation extending from the rectum to the splenic flexure.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Swelling and frothy urine
questions.vignette: A 30-year-old woman presents with puffiness around the eyes, generalised oedema and frothy urine. BP is normal. Urine protein is 5 g/24 h with no haematuria, serum albumin 2.1 g/dL and cholesterol is raised.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Joint pain and rash
questions.vignette: A 32-year-old woman has symmetrical small-joint pain in the hands, a photosensitive rash across the cheeks and nose, and painless oral ulcers. ANA and anti-dsDNA antibodies are positive and complement levels are low.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Painful big toe
questions.vignette: A 55-year-old obese man wakes with excruciating pain, swelling and redness of the first metatarsophalangeal joint after a night of heavy eating and drinking. He is afebrile. He takes a thiazide diuretic.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Tiredness and weight gain
questions.vignette: A 48-year-old woman reports tiredness, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation and dry skin. HR 54/min, with slow-relaxing ankle reflexes. TSH is markedly raised and free T4 is low. Anti-TPO antibodies are positive.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Barking cough
questions.vignette: An 18-month-old child has a barking cough, hoarse voice and inspiratory stridor that is worse at night, following two days of runny nose and low-grade fever. The child is alert and not drooling.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Wheezy infant
questions.vignette: A 6-month-old infant has two days of runny nose followed by cough, wheeze, fine crackles and fast breathing during winter. The infant is feeding poorly. SpO2 93%. There is no previous history of wheeze.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Prolonged fever with red eyes
questions.vignette: A 4-year-old child has had fever for 6 days, bilateral non-purulent conjunctival injection, red cracked lips, a strawberry tongue, unilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and swelling of the hands and feet.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Pain and spotting in early pregnancy
questions.vignette: A 26-year-old woman with 7 weeks of amenorrhoea has lower abdominal pain on the left and vaginal spotting. Urine hCG is positive. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an empty uterus and a left adnexal mass with free fluid.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Headache in late pregnancy
questions.vignette: A 32-year-old primigravida at 34 weeks' gestation reports severe headache and flashing lights. BP 164/110 mmHg, urine protein 3+, brisk reflexes and oedema of the face and hands. She has had no seizures.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Irregular periods and acne
questions.vignette: A 24-year-old woman has irregular periods since menarche, excess facial hair and acne. BMI 31 kg/m². Pelvic ultrasound shows multiple peripheral follicles in enlarged ovaries. Prolactin and TSH are normal.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Scaly plaques
questions.vignette: A 28-year-old man has well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale over the extensor surfaces of the elbows and knees and in the scalp. He has pitting of the fingernails.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Chronic cough and weight loss
questions.vignette: A 38-year-old man has a 4-week cough with occasional blood-streaked sputum, evening fevers, night sweats and 6 kg weight loss. Chest X-ray shows a cavitating lesion in the right upper lobe.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Fever with low platelets
questions.vignette: During the monsoon, a 22-year-old woman has high fever, severe body aches, pain behind the eyes and a blanching rash on day 4 of illness. Platelets 60,000/µL and haematocrit is rising. NS1 antigen is positive.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.title: Persistent low mood
questions.vignette: A 29-year-old woman reports 2 months of persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities, early-morning waking, poor concentration, feelings of guilt and weight loss. She has no history of elevated mood. Thyroid function is normal.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely diagnosis?
